content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Eric Woods (E019) requests write access to Payroll.

Notes:
- Notes 1-5 say he's a full-time Engineer, max is write (Payroll owned by Payroll Specialist, so no admin). Recommend write.
- Note 6 (Security) says he's a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max is read (or write only with advanced training; he has basic). Recommend read.

Conflict: employment type - full_time vs contractor. Most notes say full-time, but the Security agent actually looked it up in their own database and found contractor with basic security training.

Hmm. Which to trust? The Security database is the one that actually looked up employment type in their own database. The other notes mostly looked up role but derived employment type from HR notes (which seem to say full-time). Note 6 looked up employment type in their own database and found contractor.

Actually, let's consider: HR is typically the source of truth for employment type. But the HR note (note 1) says full-time. However, the Security note says contractor with basic security training, looked up in own database.

Wait, note 1 says "employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)" - that's HR, whose own database would be the source of truth for employment. Note 2 says "employment type: full_time (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)" - IT relied on HR note. Note 4 and 5 similar. Note 6 says "employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)" - Security looked it up in their own database and found contractor.

So we have conflicting info: HR says full-time, Security says contractor. Which is more reliable for employment type? Typically HR's database is the authoritative source for employment status. But the security database apparently also has employment type.

This is a classic conflict resolution scenario. The evidence: 5 agents (incl. HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities) say full-time; 1 agent (Security) says contractor. The majority says full-time. Also HR looked it up in own database. So employment type = full-time.

Role: Engineer (consistent across all notes, looked up). Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist role. Full-time employees: up to write, admin only if role owns system. Engineer doesn't own Payroll, so max = write.

Requested write. Max = write. Grant write.

So decision: write.

Let me submit.
